Answer: C
Reason: The CT images demonstrate extensive pneumomediastinum and subcutaneous emphysema extending into the neck (retropharyngeal space), with air also visible within the spinal canal. Pneumorrhachis in this context is best explained by air tracking from the mediastinum/retropharyngeal space through the cervical neural exit foramina into the epidural space, rather than direct trauma, esophageal perforation, or isolated subcutaneous spread.
